newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Kalgold debut strikes rich vein of demand.
newsitem.headline: Kalgold debut strikes rich vein of demand.

text.p: Shares in South African gold mine Kalahari Goldridge Mining Co Ltd surged on their debut on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Monday as traders eagerly snapped up the newly-listed shares.

The stock, which was listed by introduction and so had no issue price, first traded at 370 cents -- above expectations of around 300-350. The stock quickly jumped to 400 cents before falling back to 390 cents by 1100 GMT.
"There is large demand for the shares," one analyst said.
KalGold's main asset, the Goldridge Project in North West Province, is an Archaean greenstone-hosted gold source that is rare in South Africa.
Exploration in the lease area has so far resulted in the discovery of 30 tonnes of gold with a further 33 tonnes categorised as inferred resources.
The mine is open cast and so cheaper to run and expand. Analysts said the prospects for the mine were good and that market sentiment was bullish following an analysts visit to the site last week.
"They have done some good marketing and people have a bit of faith in the project," said Henk de Hoop, gold mining analyst at BOE Natwest.
De Hoop said it was difficult to predict the exact future worth of the shares as the mine was just starting out, but had the potential to grow into a valuable resource.
Analysts compared the stock to Amalia Gold Mining and Exploration Ltd which also has a site in North West Province.
Some said KalGold could represent a safer bet with its strong quality management that has stuck rigidly to its schedule so far and the mine's good ore grade.
"It is a bit less of a risk than Amalia," one analyst said.
Analysts said some small investors could be switching their stock out of Amalia and into KalGold. Amalia shares were down six cents to 134 cents.

West Rand Consolidated Mines Ltd still holds a majority stake of 72.4 percent of KalGold and analysts said this was making KalGold stock illiquid. But with the success of the listing they predicted more stock would eventually be released onto the market.
Banking sources close to the listing said the firm was likely to issue for cash up to 9.5 million new shares at some time within the next six months.
"They will be issuing more shares soon. The initial feeling was within a year, but now the latest feeling is within six months," one source said.
